title: Business Central 29.0: Major Change to Table Extensions and SQL Storage.
summary: Business Central 29.0 changes how table extension fields are stored in the database, moving from a companion-table model to storing extension fields directly in the same SQL table as the base table. This enables cross-table indexes, can improve query performance, and requires developers to avoid direct SQL dependencies.
key_points: Extension fields now physically reside in the same SQL table as base table fields instead of separate companion tables
Developers can create indexes spanning both base table and extension fields for more flexible data access patterns
Database operations involving extensions may perform faster due to co-located storage of all fields
Partial record loading remains important despite the new storage model; developers should continue using SetLoadFields appropriately
Solutions should depend on AL and Business Central APIs rather than direct SQL, as physical schema is an implementation detail that can change

quotes.text: Developers can define indexes that span fields from a base table and its table extensions.
quotes.why_it_matters: This new capability enables more flexible data access optimization that was impossible with the previous companion-table approach
